S3.label: bug
S3.suggestionContent: WHAT: Both merges use ZUNIONSTORE default AGGREGATE SUM so a duplicate payload present in both inputs gets its end-timestamp score summed. S4.label: bug

WHY: An attacker can send far-future timestamps to pin their spans and force eviction of legitimate spans in the same segment, biasing sampling/storage. HOW: Validate/clamp the score server-side instead of trusting client time.

WHY: Building a segment span-by-span copies O(N) per insert, i.e. O(N^2) total per segment and O(B*N) per batch in the ingest hot path. HOW: Merge once per batch or skip union when keys are already joined.

S7.label: bug

S8.label: bug
S8.suggestionContent: Both ZUNIONSTORE calls merge ZSETs whose scores are end_timestamp_precise produced in buffer.py. Default AGGREGATE SUM doubles the score for any member present in both inputs (retry/duplicate payload), breaking the timestamp ordering that zpopmin eviction relies on. Specify AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN) on both merges so duplicate members keep a valid timestamp.
